rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied phrase is ‘from a favor for which recompense is due’; the ظرف is omitted for the surah’s rhyme, resolving the objection that the passive verb lacks a specified agent.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير من نعمة تجزى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: he gives his wealth only while seeking the face of his Most High Lord.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع والمعنى ولكنه يؤتي ماله طلبا لوجه ربه الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing person will be satisfied with the abundant, beautiful reward his Most High Lord gives him.
rows.anchor: ولسوف يرضى هذا الأتقى بما يؤتيه ربه الأعلى من الأجر الجزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God both Lord and Most High signals that the reward is the most blessed and elevated, fitting His lordship and exaltedness.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر صفتي الرب والأعلى إشعار بأن ما يؤتاه من الجزاء أنعم الجزاء وأعلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘his Most High Lord’ makes a rhetorical shift from first-person speech to third-person reference through the two divine attributes.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر وجه الالتفات

rows.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
rows.claim: Asked about divine oaths by created things, Imam al-Baqir answered that God may swear by any of His creatures, while creatures may swear only by God.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم قال قلت لأبي جعفر عليه السلام قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: علي بن مهزيار
rows.claim: Al-Faqih also transmits the ruling that God may swear by His creation but creatures may swear only by Him, through Ali ibn Mahziyar from Imam al-Baqir II.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الفقيه بإسناده عن علي بن مهزيار عن أبي جعفر الثاني

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: In al-Qummi’s gloss, the night covers the day, and the phrase is an oath.
rows.anchor: قال حين يغشى النهار وهو قسم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: The report tells how Abu al-Dahdah bought a harmful date palm with his garden, gave it to the Prophet, and received a palm in Paradise in exchange.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ ‘I was among the astray’ means he had not yet received the guidance of prophethood; this is compared with the Prophet’s earlier lack of knowledge of scripture and faith.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الباب قول موسى على ما حكى الله عنه فعلتها إذا وأنا من الضالين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes ضالّ as lacking knowledge, as in the verse about one woman forgetting and the other reminding her.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى وجدك ضالا بين الناس لا يعرفون حقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse ‘you were among the unaware’ before revelation supports the interpretation of ضالّ as lacking prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قوله وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the Prophet was lost among people who did not know his worth, and God guided them to recognize him.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه إشارة إلى ضلاله في طريق مكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says he was lost on the road to Mecca when Halima brought him from the desert to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: على ما روي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says he was lost in Mecca’s ravines as a child.
rows.anchor: وقيل إشارة إلى ما روي من ضلاله في شعاب مكة صغيرا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further report places the incident on his journey to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib, in Maysara Khadija’s servant’s caravan.
rows.anchor: في مسيره إلى الشام مع عمه أبي طالب في قافلة ميسرة غلام خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The road, ravines, and caravan interpretations, along with similar suggestions, are manifestly weak.
rows.anchor: وقيل غير ذلك وهي وجوه ضعيفة ظاهرة الضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿāʾil is a poor person without property; God enriched the Prophet after his marriage to Khadija, who gave him her considerable wealth.
rows.anchor: العائل الفقير الذي لا مال له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A different explanation understands ‘enriched’ as God answering the Prophet’s supplication.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالإغناء استجابة دعوته

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines قهر as both overcoming and humiliating, though it can be used for either meaning separately.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب القهر الغلبة والتذليل معا ويستعمل في كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr means rebuking someone and turning them away harshly.
rows.anchor: النهر هو الزجر والرد بغلظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking of a blessing means naming it aloud and displaying it in action; both are ways of giving thanks.
rows.anchor: التحديث بالنعمة ذكرها قولا وإظهارها فعلا وذلك شكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These commands are general obligations for people even though they are addressed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأوامر عامة للناس وإن كانت موجهة إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having known an orphan’s vulnerability, the Prophet is told not to humiliate an orphan in person or property.
rows.anchor: فلا تقهر اليتيم باستذلاله في نفسه أو ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having experienced the need for guidance and wealth, the Prophet is told not to rebuke a petitioner seeking spiritual or material help.
rows.anchor: فلا تزجر سائلا يسألك رفع حاجته إلى هدى أو معاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because what he has is a gift from his Lord, he should thank Him by speaking of and displaying the blessing rather than hiding it.
rows.anchor: فاشكر نعمته بالتحديث بها ولا تسترها

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses al-ḍuḥā as the sun after it rises and the night when it becomes dark.
rows.anchor: قال إذا ارتفعت الشمس { والليل إذا سجى } قال إذا أظلم

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains ‘He did not detest you’ as meaning that God did not hate the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفيه في قوله تعالى { وما قلى } قال لم يبغضك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage conveys the same argument as the questions whether God would equate believers and wrongdoers or the pious and immoral.
rows.anchor: أم نجعل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كالمفسدين في الأرض

rows.speaker: بعض من جعل الخطاب في فما يكذبك للنبي
rows.claim: Some take the address to the Prophet, read ما as ‘who’ and الحكم as ‘judgment,’ asking who can call the judgment-day recompense false when God will judge between him and its deniers.
rows.anchor: وبعض من جعل الخطاب في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that turns the verse into a question about who accuses the Prophet of falsehood is unnecessarily strained.
rows.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن فيه تكلفا من غير موجب

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi reports symbolic locations for the oath: the fig is Medina, the olive Jerusalem, Sinai Kufa, and the secure city Mecca.
rows.anchor: التين المدينة والزيتون بيت المقدس وطور سينين الكوفة وهذا البلد الأمين مكة

rows.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عن آبائه عن النبي
rows.claim: The same location interpretation occurs in a report through Musa ibn Jaʿfar and his forefathers from the Prophet; the author says it has problems.
rows.anchor: ورد هذا المعنى في بعض الروايات عن موسى بن جعفر عن آبائه عليهم السلام عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report identifying the fig and olive with Hasan and Husayn, Sinai with Ali, and the secure city with the Prophet is not genuine exegesis.
rows.anchor: وفي بعضها أن التين والزيتون الحسن والحسين والطور علي والبلد الأمين النبي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that Khuzayma ibn Thabit, not the Ansari, asked the Prophet about the secure city and was told it was Mecca.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أن خزيمة بن ثابت وليس بالأنصاري سأل النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah commands the Prophet to receive the Qur’an by revelation; it was the first Qur’anic surah revealed, is certainly Meccan, and its context permits a single, complete descent.
rows.anchor: بيان أمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بتلقي القرآن

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines recitation as joining letters and words in ordered reading, not merely gathering people or pronouncing a single letter.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب والقراءة ضم الحروف والكلمات بعضها إلى بعض في الترتيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaraʾa can mean mentally combining written words, uttering them aloud, or reading them to another person; in the last sense it is also tilāwa.
rows.anchor: يقال قرأت الكتاب إذا جمعت ما فيه من الحروف والكلمات بضم بعضها إلى بعض في الذهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of iqraʾ is to receive and read what the angel reveals; the command is embedded within the revealed book, like an instruction at a book’s opening.
rows.anchor: من القرآن فالجملة أمر بقراءة الكتاب وهي من الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording supports this being the first revelation and implies an omitted object, ‘the Qur’an’ or its equivalent.
rows.anchor: وهذا السياق يؤيد أولا ما ورد أن الآيات أول ما نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command does not simply use read intransitively with its object omitted, nor does it mean ‘recite to people’ with an omitted complement.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد مطلق القراءة باستعمال { اقرأ } استعمال الفعل اللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘in the name of your Lord’ is not the object of ‘read’ with an extra ba, yielding ‘read your Lord’s name’ or merely say the basmala.
rows.anchor: ولا أن قوله { باسم ربك } مفعول { اقرأ } والباء زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In the name of your Lord’ attaches to an implied ‘beginning’ or to ‘read’ with the ba of accompaniment; the basmala is part of the surah and God teaches by having the Prophet begin with it.
rows.anchor: الباء للملابسة ولا ينافي ذلك كون البسملة المبتداة بها السورة جزء من السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied exception is exemplified by the instruction not to say ‘I will do this tomorrow’ unless God wills.
rows.anchor: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Your Lord who created’ asserts that lordship belongs to God alone, refuting polytheists who concede creation but assign governance to favored angels, jinn, or humans.
rows.anchor: فدفعه الله بقوله { ربك الذي خلق } الناص على أن الربوبية والخلق له وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Humankind’ is the human species, and ʿalaq is coagulated blood—the stage to which the womb’s fertilized drop develops.
rows.anchor: المراد جنس الإنسان المتناسل والعلق الدم المتجمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human develops by successive divine governance from a clot into a complete being of astonishing traits; this shows that God is Lord because He is creator.
rows.anchor: فلم يتم الإنسان إنسانا ولم يكمل إلا بتدبير متعاقب منه تعالى وهو بعينه خلق بعد خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command to read visibly reinforces the first.
rows.anchor: أمر بالقراءة ثانيا تأكيدا للأمر الأول على ما هو ظاهر سياق الإطلاق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view distinguishes the commands: the first tells the Prophet to read privately and the second to recite to the people in proclamation.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به الأمر بالقراءة على الناس وهو التبليغ بخلاف الأمر الأول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes both commands as orders to recite the Qur’an publicly.
rows.anchor: كما قيل إن المراد بالأمرين جميعا الأمر بالقراءة على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither alternative about public recitation is apparent from the wording.
rows.anchor: والوجهان غير ظاهرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Most Generous Lord gives more than anyone else without prior entitlement; every blessing ultimately comes from Him.
rows.anchor: فهو تعالى يعطي لا عن استحقاق وما من نعمة إلا وينتهي إيتاؤها إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ba is causal: God taught reading or writing, with the pen serving as the means; the clause may be circumstantial or a fresh statement.
rows.anchor: الباء للسببية أي علم القراءة أو الكتابة والقراءة بواسطة القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage steadies the unlettered Prophet: the Lord who taught people to read by the pen can teach him the revealed book, and would not command what He could not enable.
rows.anchor: فهو قادر على أن يعلمك قراءة كتابه وأنت أمي وقد أمرك بالقراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God taught people what they did not know generalizes the blessing and further reassures the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ثم عمم سبحانه النعمة فذكر تعليمه للإنسان ما لم يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Humankind’ is generic here.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس كما هو ظاهر السياق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternative identifications of humankind are Adam, Idris as the first to write, or every prophet who wrote; the author regards them as weak and unnatural.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به آدم عليه السلام، وقيل إدريس عليه السلام لأنه أول من خط بالقلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation identifies humankind as every prophet who wrote; the author considers this and the preceding proposals remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل كل نبي كان يكتب وهي وجوه ضعيفة بعيدة عن الفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke corrects the implication that people should be grateful for blessings such as writing and revelation: instead, a person disbelieves and transgresses.
rows.anchor: فعلى الإنسان أن يشكره على ذلك لكنه يكفر بنعمته تعالى ويطغى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān means exceeding one’s bounds, and the statement describes a tendency in human nature, as in the description ‘wrongdoing, ungrateful.’
rows.anchor: وقوله { أن رآه استغنى } من الرأي دون الرؤية البصرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾā here means mental judgment, not visual sight; the human is both subject and object, and the clause explains why he transgresses: he supposes himself independent.
rows.anchor: وجملة { أن رآه استغنى } في مقام التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-sufficient person attends to himself and outward means, forgets the Lord who blessed him, and then transgresses.
rows.anchor: فيغفل عن ربه من غير أن يرى حاجة منه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rujʿā means return; in the context of the following threat it warns of death and resurrection, and the address is to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الرجعى هو الرجوع والظاهر من سياق الوعيد الآتي أنه وعيد وتهديد بالموت والبعث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A proposed emphatic reading addresses the human directly through a shift in person.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخطاب للإنسان بطريق الالتفات للتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet as the addressee is the more apparent reading.
rows.anchor: والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses give an example of the transgressing person and prepare for the threat of punishment, prohibition on obeying him, and command to worship God.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة ذكر بعض المصاديق للإنسان الطاغي وهو كالتوطئة لوعيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant being prevented from prayer is the Prophet, as the ending orders him not to obey the forbidding man and to prostrate.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعبد الذي كان يصلي هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the surah was the first revelation and came all at once, it shows the Prophet prayed before receiving the Qur’an, hence prophethood preceded his Qur’anic mission.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على نبوته قبل رسالته بالقرآن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say prayer was not prescribed at the start of the mission but began on the Night of Ascension, citing the daily-prayer verse.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذكره بعضهم أنه لم تكن الصلاة مفروضة في أول البعثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ascension reports establish only that the five daily prayers in their specific two-rakʿah form were prescribed then, not that prayer had never been prescribed earlier.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة فيها على عدم تشريعها قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier Meccan surahs including al-Muddaththir and al-Muzzammil mention prayer, whose known form included some Qur’an recitation and prostration.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في كثير من السور المكية ومنها النازلة قبل سورة الإسراء كالمدثر والمزمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports say the Prophet prayed with Khadija and Ali early in the mission, though they do not describe the prayer’s form.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في بعض الروايات صلاة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مع خديجة وعلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arayta means ‘tell me’ and expresses astonishment; the author assigns different first objects to its three occurrences but a common second object, ‘did he not know that God sees?’
rows.anchor: وبالجملة قوله { أرأيت } بمعنى أخبرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions ask how the forbidding man fares if the praying servant follows guidance or commands piety, and whether a denier who forbids prayer deserves anything but punishment while knowing God sees.
rows.anchor: هل يستحق إلا العذاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative parse makes the relative person, or its pronoun, the first object of all three ‘tell me’ clauses.
rows.anchor: وقيل المفعول الأول لأرأيت في جميع المواضع الثلاث هو الموصول أو الضمير العائد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that alternative parse, the clause asks what the forbidding man should have done if the servant was guided; the author says the reading is remote.
rows.anchor: أخبرني عن هذا الناهي إن كان على الهدى أو أمر بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That interpretation is remote; the differing pronouns may be parsed separately, as the context and its clues support.
rows.anchor: ولا بأس بالتفكيك بين الضمائر مع مساعدة السياق وإعانة القرائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that God sees follows by implication from belief that He created everything and therefore knows and can do everything; polytheists acknowledged these divine attributes despite their negligence.
rows.anchor: لازم الاعتقاد بأن الله خالق كل شيء هو الاعتقاد بأن له علما بكل شيء

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines safʿ as seizing and pulling something with great force.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع والسفع الجذب الشديد يقال سفعت بالشيء إذا قبضت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the forehead deceitful and sinful is figurative: those qualities belong to its owner.
rows.anchor: وفي توصيف الناصية بالكذب والخطأ وهما وصفا صاحب الناصية مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means that, if the man does not stop forbidding prayer, God will seize him by the forehead and drag him into punishment in humiliation; its owner lies and sins.
rows.anchor: لنأخذن بناصيته أخذ الذليل المهان ونجذبنه إلى العذاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands the threat as burning and blackening the forehead with fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لنسفعن ناصيته بالنار ونسودنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nādī means the council or meeting place, and here likely the people who gather there; the command is a challenge to summon them for help.
rows.anchor: النادي المجلس وكأن المراد به أهل المجلس أي الجمع الذي يجتمع بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes nādī to mean an individual companion or fellow-sitter.
rows.anchor: وقيل الجليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zabāniya are angels assigned to Hell, stern wardens against whom human help will be useless.
rows.anchor: والزبانية الملائكة الموكلون بالنار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further lexical view says zabāniya means policemen in the language of the people.
rows.anchor: وقيل الزبانية في كلامهم الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed rebuke adds emphasis; ‘do not obey him’ means do not obey his ban on prayer, as the following command to prostrate shows that sajda here is prayer.
rows.anchor: تكرار الردع للتأكيد، وقوله { لا تطعه } أي لا تطعه في النهي عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s prayer at that time may have consisted of glorifying God and prostrating to Him.
rows.anchor: ولعل الصلاة التي كان صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يأتي بها يومئذ كانت تسبيحه تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the command as prostration upon reciting this surah, one of the Qur’an’s four obligatory prostrations.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به السجود لقراءة هذه السورة التي هي إحدى العزائم الأربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtirāb means drawing near to God.
rows.anchor: والاقتراب التقرب إلى الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes ‘draw near’ to mean approaching God’s reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاقتراب من ثواب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
rows.claim: Aisha recounts the first revelation: true dreams and retreat at Hira, Gabriel’s repeated embrace and recitation, Khadija’s reassurance, Waraqa’s identification of Moses’ angel and warning of persecution, then a pause before al-Muddaththir.
rows.anchor: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
rows.claim: Ibn Shaddad reports Gabriel repeatedly ordered the Prophet to read and embraced him when he replied he could not.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد قال أتى جبريل محمدا صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال يا محمد اقرأ

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The cited Prophet report says a servant is closest to God while prostrating.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع في الحديث عن عبد الله بن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is problematic because it depicts the Prophet doubting revelation and fearing demonic possession, then accepting prophethood through a Christian ascetic’s unsupported word.
rows.anchor: والقصة لا تخلو من شيء وأهون ما فيها من الإشكال شك النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic revelation and messengership necessarily give the Prophet certainty that the message comes from God, as reports from the Imams of the Prophet’s family state.
rows.anchor: والحق أن وحي النبوة والرسالة يلازم اليقين من النبي والرسول بكونه من الله

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ says Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet’s neck while he prayed, but retreated before a fiery trench and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him if he approached. Muslim records it.
rows.anchor: إن أبا جهل قال هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين اظهركم

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira as the man who prevented people from praying and obeying God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: كان الوليد بن المغيرة ينهى الناس عن الصلاة وأن يطاع الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qummi’s identification does not fit the apparent context, where the person praying is the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أقول مفاده لا يلائم ظهور سياق الآيات في كون المصلي هو النبي

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: Imam al-Rida likewise says the servant is nearest to God when prostrating, and connects this to ‘prostrate and draw near.’
rows.anchor: سمعت الرضا عليه السلام يقول أقرب ما يكون العبد من الله وهو ساجد

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq names four obligatory prostrations of recitation—al-Sajda, Ha Mim Sajda, al-Najm, and al-ʿAlaq—and says other Qur’anic prostrations are recommended.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع روى عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال العزائم الم التنزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah describes the Qur’an’s descent on the Night of Power, its superiority to a thousand months, and the descent of angels and the Spirit; it may be Meccan or Medinan, though some occasion reports favor Medinan.
rows.anchor: تذكر السورة إنزال القرآن في ليلة القدر وتعظم الليلة بتفضيلها على ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the whole Qur’an: anzāl suggests a complete descent at once, unlike tanzīl’s gradual descent.
rows.anchor: وظاهره جملة الكتاب العزيز لا بعض آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogous wording in 44:2-3 speaks of the complete revealed Book, supporting a collective descent to the Prophet distinct from its gradual revelation over twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: وفي معنى الآية قوله تعالى والكتاب المبين إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that ‘We sent it down’ only means beginning the descent of part of the Qur’an is not supported by God’s wording.
rows.anchor: فلا يعبأ بما قيل إن معنى قوله { أنزلناه } ابتدأنا بإنزاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together with 2:185, the verse places the Night of Power in Ramadan; reports specify the particular night.
rows.anchor: فإن الآية بانضمامها إلى آية القدر تدل على أن الليلة من ليالي شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qadr most plausibly means determination: God decrees the coming year’s events on this night, as 44:4-6 explains.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالقدر التقدير فهي ليلة التقدير يقدر الله فيها حوادث السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annual decree covers life and death, provision, happiness and misery, and other events until the same night the following year.
rows.anchor: من حياة وموت ورزق وسعادة وشقاء وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Night of Power recurs each Ramadan, determining the year’s events; ‘He distinguishes’ is present tense, while the verses on its value and angelic descent support recurrence.
rows.anchor: أن الليلة متكررة بتكرر السنين ففي شهر رمضان من كل سنة قمرية ليلة تقدر فيها أمور السنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One rejected view makes the Night of Power a single historical night on which the Qur’an descended without recurring.
rows.anchor: فلا وجه لما قيل إنها كانت ليلة واحدة بعينها نزل فيها القرآن من غير أن يتكرر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another rejected view says the night recurred only during the Prophet’s lifetime and was later lifted.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إنها كانت تتكرر بتكرر السنين في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ثم رفعها الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further rejected view makes the night a fixed date somewhere in the year.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إنها واحدة بعينها في جميع السنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another rejected view says its date changes between Ramadan, Shaʿban, or other months from year to year.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إنها في جميع السنة غير أنها تتبدل بتكرر السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These positions conflict with the continuing annual decree and the present-tense description of angelic descent; one recurring Ramadan night each year is the coherent reading.
rows.anchor: فلا وجه لما قيل إنها كانت ليلة واحدة بعينها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative derives qadr from rank: the night is named for its importance or for the rank of those worshipping in it.
rows.anchor: وقيل القدر بمعنى المنزلة وإنما سميت ليلة القدر للاهتمام بمنزلتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative derives qadr from constriction, because angels’ descent makes the earth crowded.
rows.anchor: وقيل القدر بمعنى الضيق وسميت ليلة القدر لضيق الأرض فيها بنزول الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rank and constriction etymologies are weak compared with qadr meaning determination.
rows.anchor: والوجهان كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Annual determination does not preclude changes in how decreed events unfold, nor changes under divine will from what is fixed in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي ذلك وقوع التغير فيها بحسب التحقق في ظرف السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Determination has degrees according to whether causes and conditions are complete; a decree may begin on the night and reach completion later, though the reports do not support this proposal.
rows.anchor: ومن المحتمل أن تقع في ليلة القدر بعض مراتب الإحكام ويتأخر تمام الإحكام إلى وقت آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What makes you know?’ is a formula stressing the night’s greatness; repeating ‘Night of Power’ instead of a pronoun intensifies its grandeur.
rows.anchor: كناية عن جلالة قدر الليلة وعظم منزلتها ويؤكد ذلك إظهار الاسم مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night surpasses a thousand months in the merit of worship: reviving it in worship is better than worship over a thousand months, consistent with the Qur’an’s aim of drawing people to God.
rows.anchor: خيريتها منها من حيث فضيلة العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanazzalu derives from tatanazzalu; the apparent meaning of al-rūḥ is the Spirit that belongs to the divine Command.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من الروح هو الروح الذي من الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s permission means leave or notice that no impediment exists.
rows.anchor: والإذن في الشيء الرخصة فيه وهو إعلام عدم المانع منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take min in ‘from every command’ as meaning bi, while another view marks an origin or cause and a further view gives the purpose of managing every affair.
rows.anchor: قيل بمعنى الباء وقيل لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If amr means God’s creative command ‘Be,’ min marks origin and causation: the angels’ descent begins from, and issues from, every divine command.
rows.anchor: فمن للابتداء وتفيد السببية والمعنى تتنزل الملائكة والروح في ليلة القدر بإذن ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If amr means created events, min gives their purpose: angels and Spirit descend to administer each cosmic affair.
rows.anchor: فمن بمعنى اللام التعليلية والمعنى تتنزل الملائكة والروح في الليلة بإذن ربهم لأجل تدبير كل أمر

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines salām as being free of outward and inward afflictions.
rows.anchor: قال في المفردات السلام والسلامة التعري من الآفات الظاهرة والباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘It is peace’ signals God’s mercy to those who turn to Him and closure against a fresh punishment specific to the night, weakening the devils’ designs as some reports suggest.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى العناية الإلهية بشمول الرحمة لعباده المقبلين إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the angels greet each believing worshipper they pass; this amounts to the same idea of divine care.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به أن الملائكة يسلمون على من مروا به من المؤمنين المتعبدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descriptions of angelic descent and peace explain why the Night of Power is better than a thousand months.
rows.anchor: والآيتان أعني قوله { تنزل الملائكة } إلى آخر السورة

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Asked whether the Night of Power ended with the prophets, the Prophet answered that it remains until the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال قلت يا رسول الله القدر القدر شيء يكون على عهد الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Similar reports also come through Sunni transmission routes.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه غير واحد من الروايات من طرق أهل السنة

rows.speaker: حسان بن أبي علي
rows.claim: Asked Imam al-Sadiq when to seek the Night of Power, Hassan ibn Abi Ali was told to seek it on the nineteenth, twenty-first, and twenty-third nights.
rows.anchor: عن حسان بن أبي علي قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن ليلة القدر قال اطلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports narrow the search to the twenty-first and twenty-third; traditions point especially to the twenty-third, whose date may be concealed so people do not treat it lightly by sinning.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار الترديد بين ليلتين الإحدى والعشرين والثلاث والعشرين

rows.speaker: زرارة
rows.claim: A report from an Imam says the twenty-third is Laylat al-Juhani: the Juhani, identified as ʿAbd Allah ibn Anis al-Ansari, lived far away and the Prophet directed him to that night.
rows.anchor: في رواية عبد الله بن بكير عن زرارة عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال ليلة ثلاث وعشرين هي ليلة الجهني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of al-Juhani is also transmitted in Sunni works, including al-Durr al-Manthur from Malik and al-Bayhaqi.
rows.anchor: مروي من طرق أهل السنة أيضا أورده في الدر المنثور عن مالك والبيهقي

rows.speaker: زرارة
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq says determination occurs on the nineteenth, confirmation on the twenty-first, and execution on the twenty-third; other reports agree.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام التقدير في تسع عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Household reports agree that the Night of Power remains each year in Ramadan and is one of these three nights; Sunni reports differ markedly, with the familiar view assigning it to the twenty-seventh.
rows.anchor: فقد اتفقت أخبار أهل البيت عليهم السلام أنها باقية متكررة كل سنة

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: Al-Khatib reports from Ibn al-Musayyib that the Prophet saw the Umayyads ascending his pulpit, was distressed, and then the Night of Power surah was revealed; similar accounts come via Ibn Abbas and other transmitters.
rows.anchor: أخرج الخطيب عن ابن المسيب قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shia reports say God consoled the Prophet by granting the Night of Power, better than a thousand months—the length of Umayyad rule.
rows.anchor: سلى نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بإعطاء ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: سعيد السمان
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq explains that deeds performed on this night surpass deeds over a thousand months without a Night of Power.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال له بعض أصحابنا ولا أعلمه إلا سعيد السمان

rows.speaker: حمران
rows.claim: Imam al-Baqir says the blessed night is the recurring Night of Power in Ramadan’s last ten days, when the Qur’an descended and each coming year’s good and evil, obedience and sin, birth, death, and provision are decreed, while God retains will over the decree.
rows.anchor: عن حمران أنه سأل أبا جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: حمران
rows.claim: Imam al-Baqir explains that prayer, zakat, and every good deed on the Night of Power outweigh the same deeds over a thousand months without it; God multiplies believers’ good deeds.
rows.anchor: والعمل الصالح فيها من الصلاة والزكاة وأنواع الخير خير من العمل في ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s retained will expresses His absolute power: He can reverse even a final decree, though He will never choose to do so.
rows.anchor: فله أن ينقض القضاء المحتوم وإن كان لا يشاء ذلك أبدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet describes angels from Sidrat al-Muntaha descending with Gabriel and banners, greeting believers at sacred sites except habitual drinkers, pork eaters, and those stained with saffron.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع روى ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: أبو بصير
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq says an Imam receives an increase of the Spirit on the Night of Power; the Spirit is greater than the angel Gabriel, as the verse distinguishes the two.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال كنت مع أبي عبد الله عليه السلام فذكر شيئا من أمر الإمام إذا ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reports discuss the night and its merit; signs such as a rayless sunrise and mild air are neither constant nor prevalent, so the author omits them.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرت في بعضها لها علامات ليست بدائمة ولا أكثرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah establishes Muhammad’s message to all People of the Book, polytheists, and humanity, as divine guidance requires; it argues that the call promotes sound belief and social action.
rows.anchor: رسالة محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لعامة أهل الكتاب والمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah may be Meccan or Medinan, but its style more closely resembles a Medinan surah.
rows.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية وإن كان سياقها بالمدنية أشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is the clear proof required by divine guidance; those who disbelieved in his Islamic call among the People of the Book and polytheists could not be left without it.
rows.anchor: أن الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من مصاديق الحجة البينة القائمة على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those who disbelieved’ means those who rejected the Islamic prophetic call; min is partitive, and the polytheists are non-scriptural idolaters and others.
rows.anchor: الكافرون بالدعوة النبوية الإسلامية من أهل الكتاب والمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munfakkīn means separating from a close attachment; here they remained bound to the demands of guidance until the proof arrived and then were left to themselves.
rows.anchor: من الانفكاك وهو الانفصال عن شدة اتصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not mislead a people after guiding them until He clarifies what they must avoid.
rows.anchor: وما كان الله ليضل قوما بعد إذ هداهم حتى يبين لهم ما يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina means an evident proof; the verse’s future wording says unbelievers would remain attached to their stance until Muhammad came, who is himself the proof.
rows.anchor: والبينة هي الحجة الظاهرة والمعنى لم يكن الذين كفروا برسالة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading fits the surah’s sequence without contradiction, despite the many difficult and divergent interpretations others have proposed.
rows.anchor: والذي أوردناه من المعنى هو الذي يلائمه سياقها من غير تناقض بين الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger reciting purified pages is certainly Muhammad; ṣuḥuf are sheets and here the revealed portions of the Qur’an, as elsewhere in scripture language.
rows.anchor: المراد به محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pages are purified of falsehood touched by devils; God repeatedly says revelation is truth protected from their intrusion.
rows.anchor: تقدسها من قذارة الباطل بمس الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kutub may refer to writing, its medium, the words or meanings inscribed, or rulings and decrees; scripture uses ‘written’ for obligatory rulings.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالكتب التي في الصحف الأحكام والقضايا الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qayyima means preserving and caring for a matter; the divine rulings are upright because they sustain society, guard its interests, and secure its well-being.
rows.anchor: فإنها من القيام بالشيء بمعنى حفظه ومراعاة مصلحته وضمان سعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof was a messenger from God reciting heavenly pages cleansed of falsehood whose rulings and judgments sustain human society and preserve its interests.
rows.anchor: الحجة البينة التي أتتهم رسول من الله يقرأ صحائف سماوية مطهرة من دنس الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verse addresses rejection of Muhammad and his book, while this verse recalls earlier disputes among scripture recipients before the Islamic message.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تشير إلى اختلافهم السابق على الدعوة الإسلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof reached them through prophetic clarification in their own scripture or through their prophets, as Jesus explained matters over which they differed.
rows.anchor: ومجيء البينة لهم هو البيان النبوي الذي تبين لهم في كتابهم أو أوضحه لهم أنبياؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may include polytheists too: the Qur’an distinguishes ‘People of the Book’ from ‘those given scripture,’ the latter being broader and extending to humanity.
rows.anchor: شاملا للمشركين كما هو شامل لأهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity first disputed over social life and then religion after truth was clear; some forgot scripture, some distorted it, and some preserved and believed it.
rows.anchor: فعامة البشر آتاهم الله كتابا ثم اختلفوا فيه فمنهم من نسي ما أوتيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture was given to settle people’s disputes, yet recipients divided after clear proofs out of envy; this shows that ‘those given scripture’ includes polytheists as well as the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: ما اختلف فيه إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغيا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even after messengers and clear signs, people after them divided into believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولو شاء الله ما اقتتل الذين من بعدهم من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command applies to the disbelievers of the People of the Book and polytheists: Muhammad’s message and upright scripture call only for sincere worship without associating partners.
rows.anchor: للذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين أي لم يتضمن رسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanīf derives from turning away from both extremes toward the middle; Islam is so named because it calls for moderation throughout life.
rows.anchor: من الحنف وهو الميل عن جانبي الإفراط والتفريط إلى حاق وسط الاعتدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakat are particular items named after the general command, or parts named after the whole, to emphasize them as pillars: devotional orientation to God and spending wealth for Him.
rows.anchor: من قبيل ذكر الخاص بعد العام أو الجزء بعد الكل اهتماما بأمره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: ‘The religion of the upright scripture’ may refer to the shared religion prescribed in the heavenly books from Noah onward.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكتب القيمة إن كان جميع الكتب السماوية أعني كتاب نوح ومن دونه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the commands in the scripture Muhammad recites, whose sound rulings preserve human society’s interests.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد به ما كان يتلوه النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الكتب القيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either way, the Qur’an’s monotheistic religion confirms prior scripture and governs human life while preserving society’s welfare, as 30:30 explains.
rows.anchor: فالآية على أي حال تشير إلى كون دين التوحيد الذي يتضمنه القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine law of guidance required the proof to reach all who rejected the call; if the message reaches some People of the Book or polytheists, it must reach all.
rows.anchor: من الضروري أن لا فرق بين البعض والبعض في تعلق الدعوة فتعلقها بالبعض لا ينفك عن تعلقها بالكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage identifies Muhammad as the proof, says previous divisions followed the proof’s arrival, and shows that the commanded religion protects society’s interests.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن تلك البينة محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers among the People of the Book and polytheists will abide forever in Hell and are the worst of creation.
rows.anchor: في نار جهنم خالدين فيها أولئك هم شر البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do good are the best of creation; goodness is restricted to them just as evil is restricted to disbelievers in the previous verse.
rows.anchor: فيه قصر الخيرية في المؤمنين الصالحين كما أن في الآية السابقة قصر الشرية في الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdn means settled permanence; ‘Gardens of Eden’ already implies abiding, so ‘forever’ reinforces their permanence.
rows.anchor: العدن الاستقرار والثبات فجنات عدن جنات خلود ودوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s satisfaction is an active attribute realized in the reward He gives believers for faith and good works.
rows.anchor: الرضى منه تعالى صفة فعل ومصداقه الثواب الذي أعطاهموه جزاء لايمانهم وعملهم الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of God marks afterlife felicity: knowledge of God produces fear, which yields faith as inward commitment to His lordship and divinity, then righteous action.
rows.anchor: فالعلم بالله يستتبع الخشية منه، والخشية منه تستتبع الإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpretations of the verse’s individual words differ sharply, but the author sees no value in listing them and directs readers to longer commentaries.
rows.anchor: لهم في تفسير مفردات هذه الآيات اختلافا شديدا وأقوالا كثيرة لا جدوى في التعرض لها

rows.speaker: أبو الجارود
rows.claim: Abu al-Jarud transmits Imam al-Baqir’s identification of the clear proof as Muhammad, the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال البينة محمد رسول الله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Asked who is most honored by God, the Prophet asks Aisha whether she reads the verse naming believers who do good as the best of creation.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت قلت يا رسول الله من أكرم الخلق على الله

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet said Ali and his followers will triumph on Judgment Day when Ali approached; the verse was then revealed, and Companions called Ali ‘the best of creation.’
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال كنا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فأقبل علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A similar identification of the best of creation with Ali’s followers is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas and from Ali through several cited works.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عدي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: يزيد بن شراحيل
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Sharahil reports Ali’s account that, as the Prophet died resting on Ali’s chest, he identified Ali’s followers as the verse’s best of creation and promised their meeting at the Pool.
rows.anchor: عن يزيد ابن شراحيل الأنصاري كاتب علي عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ transmits from Ibn Abbas, through Muqatil and al-Dahhak, that ‘the best of creation’ was revealed about Ali and his household.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { هم خير البرية } قال نزلت في علي وأهل بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah describes resurrection, people’s return for recompense, and signs including the earthquake and the earth recounting its news; it may be Meccan or Medinan.
rows.anchor: ذكر للقيامة وصدور الناس للجزاء وإشارة إلى بعض أشراطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zilzāl is a verbal noun; attaching it to the earth emphasizes this earth’s particular quake and thus its ultimate severity and horror.
rows.anchor: وإضافته إلى ضمير الأرض تفيد الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athqāl may mean goods, a traveler’s baggage, or burdens; what the earth expels may be the dead, buried treasures and minerals, or all of these.
rows.anchor: الأثقال جمع ثقل بفتحتين بمعنى المتاع أو خصوص متاع المسافر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the earth’s burdens are the dead; another says they are treasures and minerals; a third includes both.
rows.anchor: الموتى على ما قيل أو الكنوز والمعادن التي في بطنها أو الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead are the best reading, followed by both dead and buried wealth, since the latter also points to resurrection for judgment.
rows.anchor: وأول الوجوه أقربها ثم الثالث لتكون الآية إشارة إلى خروجهم للحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people’s departure refers to their setting out for recompense.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى انصرافهم إلى الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human asks what is happening to the earth in stunned amazement at its tremendous earthquake.
rows.anchor: أي يقول مدهوشا متعجبا من تلك الزلزلة الشديدة الهائلة ما للأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view restricts ‘the human’ to a disbeliever who denies resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالإنسان الكافر غير المؤمن بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth testifies to human deeds, like people’s limbs, the record-keeping angels, and other witnesses.
rows.anchor: فتشهد على أعمال بني آدم كما تشهد بها أعضاؤهم وكتاب الأعمال من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lam means ‘to’: God revealed to the earth that it should speak, and it senses and bears good and evil deeds until commanded to testify on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: اللام بمعنى إلى لأن الايحاء يتعدى بإلى والمعنى تحدث أخبارها بسبب أن ربك أوحى إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s speech implies that life and awareness permeate all things, though humans fail to perceive their glorification and testimony.
rows.anchor: أن الحياة والشعور ساريان في الأشياء وإن كنا في غفلة من ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some debate whether the earth speaks through newly given life and awareness, a created voice, or by the condition of its deeds serving as testimony.
rows.anchor: أهو بإعطاء الحياة والشعور للأرض الميتة حتى تخبر بما وقع فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These competing accounts are unnecessary given the preceding explanation, and this kind of testimony need not be treated as the means by which proof is completed against a person.
rows.anchor: ولا محل لهذا الاختلاف بعد ما سمعت ولا أن الحجة تتم على أحد بهذا النوع من الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣudūr is the departure of camels from water after arriving; ashtāt means scattered groups, and the verse answers the opening ‘when’ after an earlier answer.
rows.anchor: الصدور انصراف الإبل عن الماء بعد وروده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People leave the gathering in separate groups for their homes in Paradise or Hell, the felicitous distinguished from the wretched; seeing deeds may mean seeing their recompense by inhabiting it or seeing deeds themselves embodied.
rows.anchor: انصرافهم عن الموقف إلى منازلهم في الجنة والنار وأهل السعادة والفلاح منهم متميزون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says people emerge from graves to the gathering, distinguished by features such as dark or bright faces and fear or safety, to learn their recompense through the reckoning.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به خروجهم من قبورهم إلى الموقف متفرقين متميزين بسواد الوجوه وبياضها
